units.why: The sample statement says AI use 'without citation, documentation, or authorization' is covered by academic honesty rules, classing unauthorized AI use as an honesty breach: P36.

units.passage: If there is strong suspicion or evidence of AI use in a submission, it may be reported as an academic integrity violation in accordance with Article 6 of the USU Student Code , which outlines due process for instructors and students, including options for appeal.
units.why: 'If there is strong suspicion or evidence of AI use in a submission, it may be reported as an academic integrity violation': unauthorized AI as misconduct, P36.

units.passage: B. Cheating: A form of dishonesty in which a student misrepresents their mastery of the course content or clinical experience.
units.policy: Submitting an assignment generated by AI without explicit permission is an example of cheating, a form of dishonesty in which a student misrepresents their mastery of the course content.
units.why: The same item places AI-generated submission under the heading "Cheating", a form of dishonesty, so unauthorized AI work is academic misconduct. P36 fits because it classifies the act; the explicit-permission fallback is coded separately as P06.
units.fit_note: The policy names AI only in one example item under cheating; the classification is general and the AI link comes from example 3. The anchor alone is the definition; the AI example is item 3 beneath the list header.

units.passage: Violations of this standard constitute cheating. Please note: Course expectations may vary from instructor to instructor.
units.why: 'Violations of this standard constitute cheating' places violations of the cheating standard, which contains the AI sentence, under academic dishonesty. P36 fits as AI use the instructor has not allowed is handled as misconduct.
units.fit_note: The sentence does not name AI itself; AI follows through the cheating standard in the same paragraph.

units.passage: If you do not first request permission, using such tools will be considered a violation of Penn’s Code of Academic Integrity.
units.why: 'If you do not first request permission, using such tools will be considered a violation of Penn's Code' makes use without permission a violation. P36 fits.
units.fit_note: Sample from another university.

units.passage: Doing so is considered a violation of the cheating and plagiarism standards of the UVM Code of Academic Integrity.
units.why: 'Doing so is considered a violation of the cheating and plagiarism standards of the UVM Code' classes the ban as misconduct. P36 fits.

units.passage: If a student has another person/entity do the writing of any substantive portion of an assignment for them, which includes hiring a person or a company to write essays and drafts and/or other assignments, research-based or otherwise, and using artificial intelligence affordances like ChatGPT…” [it is] considered a violation of academic integrity by the Composition Program
units.why: The UCI sample treats 'using artificial intelligence affordances like ChatGPT' as 'a violation of academic integrity by the Composition Program'. P36 fits.

units.passage: Content generated by an Artificial Intelligence third-party service or site (AI-generated content) without proper attribution or authorization is another form of plagiarism.
units.why: 'Content generated by an Artificial Intelligence third-party service or site (AI-generated content) without proper attribution or authorization is another form of plagiarism' defines misuse as plagiarism. P36 fits.
units.fit_note: Sample from another university.

units.passage: Academic dishonesty takes place whenever anyone undermines the academic integrity of the institution; represents as their work that they have not done themselves, including work generated through unsanctioned and/or undocumented artificial intelligence (A.I.) assistance; or attempts to gain an unfair advantage over others.
units.why: Academic dishonesty includes representing as one's own work "work generated through unsanctioned and/or undocumented artificial intelligence (A.I.) assistance"; AI is barred only when unsanctioned or undocumented, so P36, must-not, restrict.

units.passage: Students must follow faculty-issued instructions for courses and assignments and may be penalized or found in violation of the Code of Academic Integrity if they do not.
units.why: Students who do not follow faculty instructions "may be penalized or found in violation of the Code"; misuse becomes an integrity violation, P36.
units.fit_note: Does not name AI; applies to any faculty-issued instructions, which include AI rules.

units.passage: This includes work generated by or originating from non-human sources, such as A.I.
units.why: Plagiarism "includes work generated by or originating from non-human sources, such as A.I."; AI-generated work is classed as plagiarism, P36.

units.passage: Unacknowledged appropriation involves using either the work of another person or of A.I. without reference or acknowledgement.
units.why: "Unacknowledged appropriation involves using either the work of another person or of A.I. without reference or acknowledgement"; AI use without acknowledgement is plagiarism, so P36, must-not, restrict (acknowledged use is not barred).

units.passage: Using Gen-AI for completing coursework in ways that are prohibited by the course instructor may be a violation of the Honor Code.
units.policy: Using Gen-AI for coursework in ways prohibited by the course instructor may be a violation of the Honor Code.
units.why: "Using Gen-AI for completing coursework in ways that are prohibited by the course instructor may be a violation of the Honor Code" ties instructor rules to integrity enforcement, P36.

units.passage: You should always critically assess the responses generated by the tools and check factual claims against reliable sources. Presenting work produced by Gen-AI as one’s own or using Gen-AI for coursework in ways not permitted by the course instructor may be violations of the Honor Code.
units.policy: Presenting work produced by Gen-AI as one's own may be a violation of the Honor Code.
units.why: "Presenting work produced by Gen-AI as one's own" may violate the Honor Code. This is a separate rule from instructor-prohibited use in the same sentence; P36.
units.fit_note: Framed as an Honor Code violation (P36) rather than a flat ban.

units.passage: Presenting work produced by Gen-AI as one’s own or using Gen-AI for coursework in ways not permitted by the course instructor may be violations of the Honor Code.
units.why: "Using Gen-AI for coursework in ways not permitted by the course instructor may be violations of the Honor Code" is the student-addressed misconduct rule (P36).

units.passage: Using Gen-AI for completing coursework in ways that are prohibited by the course instructor may be a violation of the Honor Code.
units.policy: Using Gen-AI for completing coursework in ways prohibited by the course instructor may be a violation of the Honor Code.
units.why: "may be a violation of the Honor Code" for use that the instructor prohibits. Quoted Provost excerpt, P36.

units.passage: He considers any use of generative AI output to be plagiarism and thus an Honor Code violation.
units.why: "He considers any use of generative AI output to be plagiarism and thus an Honor Code violation." Treats AI use as misconduct, P36, for that instructor's courses only.

units.passage: It is equally crucial to emphasize ethical applications, and to remind students that unauthorized use of these tools constitutes academic misconduct, underlining the importance of maintaining integrity when using Gen AI in academic endeavors.
units.why: The sentence says faculty should 'remind students that unauthorized use of these tools constitutes academic misconduct', an instruction to communicate the misconduct rule at the start, so P36, instructor, course-start, should. Only unauthorized use is barred, so the unit stance is restrict.

units.passage: Instances of using Gen AI-- whether unauthorized, lacking proper documentation, or inadequate citation or attribution-- are considered academic misconduct. This encompasses (but is not limited to) actions such as cheating, deception, inappropriate collaboration, and plagiarism.
units.why: "are considered academic misconduct" classifies unauthorized AI use as misconduct (cheating, deception, plagiarism), so P36.
units.fit_note: Also implies that missing documentation or citation is itself misconduct (P28 aspect).

units.passage: Using Gen AI in a way that violates an instructor’s course policies and/or guidelines violates the VCU Honor System.
units.why: The sentence says use that violates an instructor's course policies 'violates the VCU Honor System', stating the consequence of breaking the course rule: P36, student, when-misuse, informs.
units.fit_note: Also makes the instructor's course policy the thing whose violation counts.

units.passage: Using AI without permission or proper citation can lead to plagiarism or code of conduct violations.
units.why: The sentence says 'Using AI without permission or proper citation can lead to plagiarism or code of conduct violations', classing unpermitted or uncited AI use as misconduct; P36 fits, and no penalties are named so not P37. Addressed to students.
units.fit_note: Also implies AI requires permission and citation, which the type does not capture.

units.passage: The use of AI tools to draft, edit, summarize, or generate content is considered unauthorized assistance and a violation of the Honor Code.
units.policy: The use of AI tools to draft, edit, summarize, or generate content is considered unauthorized assistance and a violation of the Honor Code
units.why: Template 2 calls 'draft, edit, summarize, or generate content' 'unauthorized assistance and a violation of the Honor Code', classing AI use as misconduct (P36); it also bans editing and summarizing (P21, P105) but the classification is the operative statement.
units.fit_note: Also names drafting, editing and summarizing as banned uses, which P19/P21/P105 would capture separately.

units.passage: The unauthorized use of AI software may fall under several definitions of academic dishonesty in the Undergraduate Honor Code.
units.why: 'The unauthorized use of AI software may fall under several definitions of academic dishonesty in the Undergraduate Honor Code' classes misuse as misconduct, P36.

units.passage: Using AI in other ways will be considered academic misconduct; if you have any questions about this policy, please contact me
units.why: 'Using AI in other ways will be considered academic misconduct' classifies unauthorized use as misconduct, P36.
units.fit_note: The fallback is expressed as academic misconduct.

units.passage: Unauthorized use of artificial intelligence or online resources
units.policy: Academic misconduct may include unauthorized use of artificial intelligence or online resources.
units.why: The list of academic misconduct includes 'Unauthorized use of artificial intelligence or online resources', classifying unauthorized AI use as misconduct (P36).

units.passage: Use of unauthorized resources may be considered an Honor Code violation
units.why: 'Use of unauthorized resources may be considered an Honor Code violation' classes unauthorized AI as misconduct under the honor system, so P36; informs, addressed to students, when-misuse, restrict.

units.passage: The use of unauthorized resources to complete academic work is a violation of the Honor Code. Each individual instructor can establish policies applicable to academic work in their courses.
units.policy: The use of unauthorized resources to complete academic work is a violation of the Honor Code; the page applies this to generative AI.
units.why: 'The use of unauthorized resources to complete academic work is a violation of the Honor Code' defines unauthorized use as an Honor Code violation, so P36.

units.passage: The Provost – in consultation with the deans of William & Mary’s colleges and schools – should issue guidance to the university community addressing how the Honor Code should be applied in the context of students’ AI use.
units.why: The Provost 'should issue guidance to the university community addressing how the Honor Code should be applied in the context of students' AI use' links AI misuse to the honor code (P36); admin, before-course, should.

units.passage: The Honor Code stipulates that all non-sanctioned behaviors are violations.)
units.why: 'The Honor Code stipulates that all non-sanctioned behaviors are violations' ties unsanctioned AI use to the Honor Code, P36.

units.passage: The William & Mary Honor Code webpage and student handbook should articulate the relationship between unsanctioned AI use and the honor code. It should also provide guidelines for instructors on how to handle suspected cases of unauthorized AI use
units.why: 'should articulate the relationship between unsanctioned AI use and the honor code' says the Honor Code pages must link unsanctioned AI to the Honor Code, P36.
units.fit_note: Directs the university to publish the link between unsanctioned AI and the Honor Code.

units.passage: It is an honor code offense to use AI tools for assistance on this assignment in any way.
units.why: 'It is an honor code offense to use AI tools for assistance on this assignment in any way' makes banned use an Honor Code offense, P36.

units.passage: It is an honor code offense to submit work for grading that was produced with the aid of AI
units.why: 'It is an honor code offense to submit work for grading that was produced with the aid of AI' (P36); student, when-misuse, informs.

units.passage: It is an honor code offense to use AI tools for more than brainstorming without explicit permission
units.why: 'It is an honor code offense to use AI tools for more than brainstorming without explicit permission' (P36); student, when-misuse, informs.

units.passage: With this in mind, remember that representing work that you did not produce as your own, including work generated or materially modified by AI, constitutes academic dishonesty
units.why: 'representing work that you did not produce as your own, including work generated or materially modified by AI, constitutes academic dishonesty' classifies it as misconduct, P36.

units.passage: If an instructor suspects a student has not followed their established course guidelines on generative AI, they should address it as they would any case of suspected academic misconduct : beginning by meeting with the student to discuss concerns
units.why: 'address it as they would any case of suspected academic misconduct' places AI cases under established integrity procedures (P36).

units.passage: If an instructor does not allow the use of AI tools and they suspect a student has used them, they will invite the student to meet with them about the possible violation of UWS 14.03(1)(b) Use of Unauthorized Materials
units.policy: When an instructor does not allow AI tools and suspects a student used them, the matter is treated as a possible violation of UWS 14.03(1)(b), Use of Unauthorized Materials.
units.why: 'If an instructor does not allow the use of AI tools and they suspect a student has used them' treats unauthorized AI use as a possible violation of UWS 14.03(1)(b) Use of Unauthorized Materials (P36).
